_note: Appearance ONLY. Maps a finish_schedule material string to what it looks like, so a render can be driven from the costing schedule without that schedule growing a second job. finish_schedule_*.json stays a costing artefact: trade, material, unit rate. Nothing here is a cost and nothing there is a colour. Keys must match the `material` strings in the finish schedule exactly; an unmatched string falls back to `_default` and is reported, never silently painted.
_basis: Flat base colour plus roughness, which is all that survives without UV maps. Sources processed 2026-09-16 (see 00_Master/Model_and_Views.md) establish that an IFC model out of Bonsai carries no UV maps, that textures therefore need per-surface unwrapping by hand, and that flat white plaster 'could actually do the trick'. Roughness is the one free lever that separates a matt paint from a glazed tile, so it is set deliberately per material rather than left at a default.

_default._why: Neutral warm grey. Used for any material string with no entry here, and reported as unmatched so the gap is visible.

Primer and washable acrylic paint._why: Near-white matt emulsion. High roughness: washable acrylic still reads matt at this scale.

Moisture-resistant latex paint._why: Slightly lower roughness than the acrylic - a moisture-resistant latex has a faint sheen, which is the only visible difference between the two paints.

Waterproofing and ceramic tile._why: Glazed ceramic. Low roughness is what makes it read as tile rather than paint without a texture - the specular response, not the pattern. Joints are not modelled, so this reads as a single glazed plane.

Decorative mineral plaster._why: Very high roughness, faintly warm. Without a bump map the texture is absent, so roughness carries the whole difference.

elements._why: Surfaces the finish schedule does not price per room. The schedule covers wall finishes; a floor, a ceiling, a door leaf and a glazed opening still have to look like something or the render is unreadable.

floor._why: Mid-brown, standing in for an unchosen floor covering. NOT a decision - see 00_Master/project_decisions.md.

ceiling._why: Near-white matt, consistent with the stretch ceiling the vault expects.

window_glass._why: Stand-in only. A real window needs the glass-shadow trick - a Mix Shader between Glass and Transparent driven by Light Path > Is Shadow Ray - so that the glass blocks nothing on shadow rays and daylight actually enters. Recorded on 00_Master/Model_and_Views.md and NOT implemented here; see the open items in the render report.

context._why: Everything outside the room being rendered. Deliberately flat and unremarkable so it does not read as a finish decision.

lighting._why: The four-step formula recorded on 00_Master/Model_and_Views.md, arrived at independently by two teachers: colour management first, sun as key, sky as fill, artificial light as accent only. Kept here as data so a lighting change is an edit to this file rather than to the renderer.
lighting._sun_angle_why: The default sun is razor-sharp. Widening the angular diameter to ~30 degrees softens the shadow, which is the single change both sources make first.
lighting._sun_strength_why: Lower than the sources' 10: they light an exterior-facing scene, this is an interior lit through one or two openings and 10 blows out the window wall.
lighting._artificial_why: A ceiling luminaire, colour set by COLOUR TEMPERATURE in kelvin rather than by picking an RGB swatch - the sources are specific that the mix of cool skylight and warm lamps is what reads as real, and that an RGB swatch does not give you that. 3200 K is warm domestic. In a daylit room this is the accent the four-step formula calls for; in a WINDOWLESS room it is the only light there is, which the Bathroom proved by rendering pure black without it.
lighting._artificial_power_why: PER SQUARE METRE, not a flat wattage. A flat 75 W was calibrated on the 16.9 m2 bedroom and then blew out the 3.1 m2 bathroom completely - same number, five times the illuminance. 4.5 W/m2 is the bedroom figure back-derived and applied by area.
